title: Resource Theory of Aquaternionicity: Every Pure State Is a Replicable Resource for Exact Simulation of Arbitrary Quantum Operations
abstract: An alchemical resource theory admits a nonfree state that can be exactly replicated by free operations and whose finitely many copies enable exact simulation of arbitrary quantum instruments. The only known nontrivial examples, imaginarity and parity asymmetry, exhaust the qubit case (arXiv:2609.12988) and exhibit an all-or-nothing property: any nonmaximal resource exactly simulates only free unitaries. We introduce aquaternionicity for even-dimensional qudits $d\ge4$, based on a quaternionic structure represented by an antiunitary $Θ$ with $Θ^2=-I$. It is extremal in two senses: every pure state is alchemical, and alchemicality is maximally abundant under mixing. Within this framework, for any nontrivial $d$-dimensional resource theory and pure alchemical state $g$, the admissible pure-mixing set satisfies $\dim\mathcal M_g\le 2d-4,$ which aquaternionicity saturates for every pure state. Conversely, these two extremal properties characterize the quaternionic structure. Because every pure state is alchemical, the initial resource can be chosen to match the known noise structure. Moreover, when the noisy resource states remain within a common isotropic subspace, the same free processor works exactly for all of them while returning the resource unchanged. This enables recalibration-free exact simulation, including universal quantum computation, and is realized for standard dephasing and dissipative noise, where aquaternionicity substantially outperforms imaginarity and parity asymmetry.
summary: This paper introduces 'aquaternionicity' as a novel, highly robust resource theory for quantum qudits. It proves that this theory is extremal because every pure state is a resource and it maximizes the dimension of the mixing set. This robustness allows for recalibration-free exact quantum simulation, significantly outperforming existing theories under structured noise.
main_problem: To characterize 'alchemical resource theories'—resource theories where a nonfree state is exactly replicable by free operations and enables the exact simulation of arbitrary quantum operations.
main_result: Aquaternionicity, based on a quaternionic structure, is shown to be extremal, saturating a universal bound ($\dim M_g = 2d-4$) and enabling recalibration-free exact simulation under structured noise.
method: The authors define and compare resource theories (Imaginarity, Parity asymmetry, Aquaternionicity) using algebraic constraints ($\Theta^2=-I$) and analyze the dimension of the admissible pure-mixing set and noise-invariant supports.
model_or_system: The study uses quantum qudits of even dimension $d \geq 4$ and compares three resource theories defined by different symmetries (Imaginarity, Parity asymmetry, Aquaternionicity). The analysis is applied to structured noise models like basis dephasing and amplitude damping.

important_parameters: Even dimension $d=2n \geq 4$; the antiunitary operator $\Theta$ satisfying $\Theta^2=-I$.
main_assumptions: The advantage demonstrated is specific to structured noise classes and does not imply universal dominance over all arbitrary CPTP noise.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the concept of alchemical resource theories. It then introduces aquaternionicity for $d \geq 4$, proving its extremal properties. Finally, it demonstrates the practical advantage of aquaternionicity by analyzing its robustness against specific structured noise channels compared to other theories.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, algebraic framework for quantifying resource robustness, showing how specific symmetries (like the quaternionic structure) lead to superior performance in quantum information tasks like simulation under noise.
